narrative.overview: MatHub looks like a well-kept desk: orderly, practical, and quiet. Light and flat, with white cards on a faint blue-grey page, hairline borders, and a single desaturated blue marking what is interactive or current. Calm, plain and trustworthy.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, light, border-defined surfaces; shadow only on floating layers.
One blue accent for links, primary actions and the active nav item.
Semantic green, orange and red appear only as subtle status tints with dark readable text.
Same components on the public site and the teacher panel.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "you can act here" or "you are here". It is never used as decoration or section color.

rules.name: The Tinted Status Rule
rules.body: Status colors always appear as a pale tint with dark text of the same hue, never as a saturated fill with white text.

rules.name: The Weight Over Size Rule
rules.body: The scale is short (14, 16, 20, 24, 36). Emphasis comes from weight and ink color before another size is added.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow appears only on something that floats above the page (menu, drawer) or marks focus. Cards and tables stay flat.

dos: Do keep every control at least 40px tall (32px only for compact toolbar actions).
Do use Slate Blue (#46689f) only for interactive or "current" states.
Do express status with a pale tint and dark same-hue text.
Do keep surfaces flat with 1px hairline borders; reserve shadow for menus, the drawer and focus.
Do make list rows whole-row click targets and keep actions right-aligned.
Do assume Czech strings run longer than English; let rows and buttons wrap instead of truncating.
Do keep monitoring flags and scores visibly teacher-side only.
donts: Don't use solid red or green buttons with white text.
Don't add shadows to resting cards, tables or inputs.
Don't introduce a second accent color or decorative gradients.
Don't add new font sizes outside 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 36 without a clear structural reason.
Don't let two near-identical card styles coexist; .card and .panel should converge.
